terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Isometric: slab edges stay parallel in the reference, so the projection is orthographic. Azimuth 45 puts a corner toward the viewer; elevation ~30 matches the observed ratio of the slab side face to its top face.

objectClass.primaryType: terrain diorama slab (isometric fantasy overworld island)
objectClass.notes: A scene presented as a bounded object: a rectangular cut block whose top face carries a complete landscape. The slab boundary is what makes it an object rather than a vista, and the blue-water-over-ochre-earth cut face is its single most identity-defining surface. No metal anywhere; every material is a matte dielectric except the satin sea. Finish is HAND-PAINTED, not PBR (see localSpecSearch core.pbr-hand-painted-vs-pbr-texture): value gradients are baked into the art. The user asked for the reference look reproduced and explicitly NOT cel shading, so the route is painted albedo carried in vertex colour plus soft real lighting - never a toon gradient ramp, and never a glossy PBR read.

reasoning: Scores total 20/24. Structurally this sits at the top of `complex`: many parts, five repetition systems, twelve material layers, three hierarchy levels.

Held at `complex` rather than `ultra-complex` deliberately: the count of parts is high but each individual part is geometrically simple (a house is a box plus a prism, a conifer is a cone). Fidelity here depends on LAYOUT and PALETTE, not on microstructure per part, which is what the ultra-complex tier exists to force.
localDetailDensity is 2, not 3: the painted source resolves cliff striation, foam lines and field boundaries, but there are no pores, scratches or fasteners to enumerate.
occlusionRisk 2: three slab faces are visible and the fourth is inferable by construction, but the mountain rear, all rear-facing cliffs, and the cloud-covered mesa fortress are hidden.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required because the identity is carried by repeated systems (conifer scatter, hamlet clusters, field patchwork, shore foam, rock islets) distributed over a heightfield, not by one silhouette. A spec with a single terrain root would validate and still reproduce none of it.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: The boundary between the water band and the ochre earth on each cut face is ragged along its run, never level.
Slab corners are square and unbevelled, which is what makes the block read as cut rather than moulded.
A white band at every land/water contact, brightest at the line and dissolving outward.
Every rock stack in open water carries its own closed foam collar.
Water colour is graded by depth: deep blue offshore through cyan to pale turquoise inshore.
A turquoise shelf band sits between the foam line and open water.
Axis-aligned crop parcels tile the flat plateau tops in alternating colours.
Parcel edges are hard; no blending crosses a boundary.
Narrow tan paths wind between hamlets, visually distinct from the straight parcel edges.
Vertical grooves and cavity-darkened lines run the full height of each riser.
Grass stops dead at the riser lip with no transition.
Horizontal bedding lines follow each terrace step on the ochre highland.
The mesa steps down in discrete terraces rather than sloping.
Snow reaches further down the gullies than the ridges, so the snowline follows drainage.
Ridgelines read as angular facets rather than a smooth cone.
A pale sand band lies between lowland grass and foam, absent where cliffs meet water.
A dark gallery band circles the lighthouse below its lantern.
Cloud bases sit at or below plateau height, inside the diorama rather than behind it.
Thin horizontal streaks cross the summit.
Land is built of flat tables at discrete levels; the gap between tiers becomes the riser.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: Rendered from the reference viewpoint (isometric, ~30 deg elevation, plan rotated 45 deg so a corner faces the viewer), the model reads as the same island: same slab proportion, same landmass layout, same landmark positions, same palette.
The slab cut face shows the blue-over-ochre strata with a ragged interface.
Terrain reads as stacked plateaus with cliff risers, not as smooth hills.
All ten identity landmarks are present and in the right quadrant.
Surfaces read hand-painted and matte under soft light - NOT cel-shaded (no quantised toon bands, no ink outline) and NOT glossy PBR.

featureGroups.name: Diorama slab, cut faces and strata
qualityCriteria: Rectangular slab with sharp 90-degree corners and a flat underside.
Every side face carries a blue water band over an ochre earth stratum.
The water/earth interface is ragged along its length, never a straight line.
Slab thickness is ~0.12 of its edge length.
failureModes: slab renders as a plain box with one colour
strata interface drawn as a level band, which reads as a printed stripe
terrain spills over the cut edge instead of being sliced by it

featureGroups.name: Plateau-and-cliff landform grammar
qualityCriteria: Land is built of flat tables separated by near-vertical rock risers.
Plateau tops are flat enough to carry rectilinear field parcels.
Cliff risers are grey-violet with vertical fluting and a hard grass lip.
Coast alternates between cliff-to-water and beach-to-water; both occur.
failureModes: terrain renders as smooth rolling hills with no risers
every coast is a beach, or every coast is a cliff
fields drape over slopes instead of lying on flat tops

featureGroups.name: Sea, shallows and foam
qualityCriteria: Depth-ordered colour: deep blue offshore, cyan mid, pale turquoise shallow.
A continuous white foam band at every land/water contact, islets included.
Sea surface flush with the slab top; satin, not mirror, not matte.
failureModes: flat single-blue water with no depth gradient
missing foam line, which is what makes the coast read as a coast
mirror-like water that contradicts the painted finish

featureGroups.name: The ten identity landmarks
qualityCriteria: Mountain massif rear-centre, snow-capped, pyramidal, snow reaching down gullies.
Stone ring monument on the NW plateau.
Waterfall off the west cliff with a spray disc at its base.
Multi-arch bridge over the central strait.
Windmill with four sails plus red-roofed village, east plateau.
Castle with red conical tower caps on the central islet.
Lighthouse on the south islet.
Ochre mesa with fortress massing, rear-right.
Rock islets in open water, each carrying a conifer.
Cloud masses at and below plateau height.
failureModes: a landmark present but in the wrong quadrant
landmarks at the wrong scale relative to the slab

featureGroups.name: Hand-painted finish, explicitly not cel shading
qualityCriteria: Albedo carries the value structure (painted), lighting stays soft and broad.
No quantised toon bands and no ink outline anywhere.
No specular hotspot on any matte surface; only the sea shows a satin response.
High-key saturated palette matching the reference stops.
failureModes: toon gradient map applied, which the user explicitly rejected
flat unlit colour that loses all form

featureGroups.name: Scatter systems and their distribution rules
qualityCriteria: Conifers cluster along ridges, cliff lips and shorelines - never uniformly spread.
Houses appear in hamlets of 3-8, not singly scattered.
Field parcels tile only flat plateau tops.
Every scatter is deterministic from a seed.
failureModes: uniform tree spacing, which reads as a plantation not a landscape
props floating above or sunk into the ground

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

lights.role: Sun, high and slightly behind the viewer, matching the reference shadow direction.
Sky dome fill; keeps shadowed faces coloured rather than black.
Cool upward bounce off the sea, which is what lifts the underside of the slab.
Broad base so no surface reads as unlit.

Contact shadow and ground shadow are required: every prop must darken the terrain beneath it, and ambient occlusion deepens the cliff bases and harbour inlets. Without contact shadow a house reads as a decal painted on the hillside rather than an object standing on it. Soft PCF, 2048 map, radius 2.5 - hard-edged shadows would fight the painted finish.

shadowBehavior.note: Soft and broad. Hard-edged shadows would fight the painted finish, and an un-shadowed prop reads as a decal on the terrain rather than an object on it.

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Slab underside is flat (hidden in the single view).
Rear terrain is generated from the same recovered field as the front and is inference.
Prop counts within clusters are approximate; positions follow the reference layout.
The plan-view layout carries a height-dependent offset of a few percent of island extent.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: Slab edge length = 1.0 relative unit; slab thickness 0.12; maximum terrain height above sea level 0.09.

the aperture of the stone ring

albedo.samplingNotes: Satin, the only non-matte surface in the scene. Colour is depth-graded, not flat. Hand-painted finish, not PBR: the value structure lives in the albedo and the lighting stays broad and soft. No toon ramp and no ink outline - the user explicitly rejected cel shading - and no specular hotspot on any matte surface.

repetitionSystems.name: Conifer scatter
repetitionSystems.distribution: density-weighted by biome class from layout.json; concentrated along ridges, cliff lips and shorelines, thinned on farm parcels, absent on sand, rock, snow and water. Never uniform - uniform spacing reads as a plantation.

repetitionSystems.name: Hamlet clusters
repetitionSystems.distribution: Clusters of 3-8 houses on flat lowland near water or paths, with random yaw. Houses never appear singly and never on slopes above the parcel threshold.

repetitionSystems.name: Farm parcel patchwork
repetitionSystems.distribution: Axis-aligned rectangles tiling flat plateau tops only, in alternating crop colours with hard boundaries.

repetitionSystems.name: Rock islets
repetitionSystems.distribution: Standing in open water clear of the coast, each with one or two conifers and its own foam collar.

repetitionSystems.name: Cloud masses
repetitionSystems.distribution: Masses of 5-9 puffs on a common flat base, at and below plateau height, concentrated over water and against the mountain flanks.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

lights.role: Sun, high and slightly behind the viewer, matching the reference shadow direction.
Sky dome fill; keeps shadowed faces coloured rather than black.
Cool upward bounce off the sea, which is what lifts the underside of the slab.
Broad base so no surface reads as unlit.

Contact shadow and ground shadow are required: every prop must darken the terrain beneath it, and ambient occlusion deepens the cliff bases and harbour inlets. Without contact shadow a house reads as a decal painted on the hillside rather than an object standing on it. Soft PCF, 2048 map, radius 2.5 - hard-edged shadows would fight the painted finish.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: Strongest match. Rectangular cut block, square corners, blue water band over ochre earth on every visible face, and the interface is ragged along its run rather than a level stripe. Proportion of band to thickness reads correctly against the reference.

Terraced tables with rock risers are present and correct, and the coastline follows the reference. The massif is the failure: quantising a radial falloff still reads as concentric contour bands - a topographic model, not the reference's faceted pyramidal peak - and it occupies roughly 40% of frame height against the reference's 25%, sitting ON the island rather than rising behind it. Noise perturbation reduced but did not remove the ringing.

Depth grading and shallow banding now read after brightening, and foam follows every coast including the islets. Still short of the reference, whose turquoise shallows are wider and whose open water is lighter; the foam band is one cell wide and reads thinner than the painted surf.

All ten landmarks exist in geometry at their un-projected plan positions, and the stone ring and bridge are now legible. Castle, lighthouse, windmill, watchtowers, pier and waterfall are too small to read at the review viewpoint - in the reference they are focal points. This is a scale defect, not a missing-component defect.

Correct in kind: matte dielectric surfaces, no toon ramp, no posterised bands, no outline pass, no rim light, and the only satin response is the sea - the cel look the user rejected is absent. Short on value: the render sits darker and lower-contrast than the reference's high-key painting, so shaded faces read grey where the reference keeps them coloured.

Clustering behaviour is right - conifers follow the biome weights, hamlets come in groups of 3-8, never singles - and farm parcels now appear as rectilinear crop blocks. Density is too high: the reference's trees are larger and sparser, so its land reads as fields with woods, while this reads as continuous forest.

reviewHistory.summary: Real reconstruction from the recovered plan grid: slab strata, terraced landform, coastline, hamlets, forests, farm parcels, ten landmarks and an island-level cloud deck. Turntable gate passes (0 holes at all four azimuths after fixing riser edge mapping). Silhouette IoU 0.773 vs 0.85 threshold; aspect and scale within tolerance. Four of five critical features below threshold - massif reads as contour bands, landmarks illegible at review scale, value range darker than the reference.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions

risks.description: Toon shading is the house style of this repository, so a gradient map could be applied out of habit. The user explicitly rejected it.
risks.mitigation: painted-finish feature review target with mustPass true.

risks.description: Evenly spaced trees would read as a plantation and destroy the painted look.
A continuous heightfield naturally produces rolling hills; the reference is flat tables with risers.
risks.mitigation: elevation quantised to tiers before displacement.

risks.description: Plan recovery assumes ground height zero.
risks.mitigation: stated as approximation; landmark placement checked by quadrant, not by pixel.
